name: Jesse MacFadyen
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. No verified birth year; known as a Nitobi/PhoneGap engineer (c. 2008–2011) who later joined Adobe after the PhoneGap acquisition; early career dates and age cannot be verified.
early_history_summary: Worked as a senior developer at Nitobi (PhoneGap/Cordova origins) from about December 2008 to October 2011, then spent many years at Adobe on related mobile/web tooling. Public biographical detail and birth year are sparse.
evidence_summary: Public sources document Nitobi and Adobe engineering roles around PhoneGap/Cordova but do not establish a birth year or a dated material milestone at or before age 26. Wikipedia has no biography page.

name: Frances Allen
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Joined IBM Research as a programmer teaching Fortran in 1957 at age 25, but her defining compiler-optimization work (Harvest/Stretch leadership from 1959; seminal papers from the mid-1960s; first woman Turing Award in 2006) came after age 26.
early_history_summary: Grew up on a farm near Lake Champlain in Peru, New York, as the oldest of six; father a farmer, mother an elementary teacher. Earned a BS in mathematics (1954), taught high-school math, then completed an MS in mathematics at the University of Michigan (1957) before joining IBM to pay off student loans.
family_context_summary: Oldest of six children on a farm in Peru, New York; father a farmer, mother an elementary school teacher. Family financial status was modest enough that student loans drove the IBM job.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was an elementary teacher; no documented parental expertise in computing or compilers.
evidence_summary: Allen's early path was teaching mathematics and then joining IBM at 25 to teach Fortran while paying loans. Material compiler research leadership and publications that underpin her Turing Award came from 1959 onward (age 27+). Employment at IBM at 25 is not treated as a qualifying breakout milestone.

name: Amanda Askell
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Completed philosophy degrees and was a PhD student through most of her mid-20s; joined OpenAI in November 2018 (~age 29–30) and Anthropic in 2021; defining Claude personality/constitution work came later.
early_history_summary: Raised in Prestwick, Scotland by a teacher mother; studied philosophy (and briefly fine art) at the University of Dundee, earned a BPhil at Oxford, and a PhD in philosophy from NYU in 2018 (thesis on Pareto principles in infinite ethics). Transitioned from academia into AI safety/policy at OpenAI then Anthropic.
family_context_summary: Raised in Prestwick by her mother, a teacher. Family financial platform not documented beyond ordinary professional household.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a teacher; no documented parental AI or tech-domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Askell's public career breakout is OpenAI (2018) and Anthropic (2021) alignment work, well after age 26. By 26 she was still primarily in graduate philosophy training; no independently verified material industry or research milestone before then.

name: Dan Benjamin
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Graduated UCF in 1994 (age ~21–22); notable ventures Cork'd, PeepCode, 5by5 (founded 2010 at age ~37), and Fireside.fm (2016) all arrived well after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Rydal, Pennsylvania. Earned a B.A. in technical writing with a computer science focus from the University of Central Florida in 1994, then worked as a software developer, UI designer, and later built content and podcast platforms.
evidence_summary: Benjamin's recognition as founder of 5by5 and later Fireside.fm came in the 2010s. College graduation and early developer work around age 22 do not constitute a material, field-defining milestone by 26.

name: Robert Cailliau
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Graduated Ghent University in 1969 (age 22) and earned an MSc at Michigan in 1972 (age 25); joined CERN in December 1974 at age 27. Defining WWW collaboration with Tim Berners-Lee, first WWW conference (1994), and related work occurred in his 40s.
early_history_summary: Born in Tongeren, Belgium; moved to Antwerp in 1958. Trained as a civil/mechanical/electrical engineer at Ghent University and completed an MSc in Computer, Information and Control Engineering at the University of Michigan (1972). After Belgian Army service maintaining Fortran simulations, joined CERN's Proton Synchrotron division in 1974.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Belgian upbringing in Tongeren/Antwerp.
evidence_summary: By age 26 Cailliau had strong engineering education but had not yet joined CERN or begun hypertext/WWW work. The material milestones that define his career (CERN, WWW proposal support, first International WWW Conference) all occurred after age 26.

name: Evelyn Miralles
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Graduated Lamar University (BS Computer Graphics, 1990) and UHCL (BA CIS, 1992) and began supporting Space Shuttle/ISS work at NASA JSC around age 26; co-authorship of DOUG VR flight software and high-profile Hubble STS-61 association are dated from 1993 onward (age 27+) and 2000.
early_history_summary: Born in Caracas, Venezuela; studied computer graphics and CIS in Texas. Joined NASA Johnson Space Center's VR lab environment in the early 1990s and spent about two decades building astronaut spacewalk training systems, including co-authorship of the Dynamic Onboard Ubiquitous Graphics (DOUG) software.
evidence_summary: Starting NASA-related VR work around graduation age is early-career employment, not a verified breakout achievement by 26. Widely cited contributions (Hubble repair mission support, DOUG software, BBC 100 Women recognition) are dated later.

name: Tianon Gravi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. No verified birth year; known as a long-time Docker official-images maintainer and Debian Developer, with public prominence in the mid-2010s container ecosystem rather than a dated early-career breakout.
early_history_summary: Open-source engineer best known for maintaining Docker Library official images and as a Debian uploading developer; has held senior technology roles around Docker official images. Detailed early biography and birth year are not publicly established.
evidence_summary: Gravi is a respected container/Debian maintainer, but without a documented birth year or a specific dated milestone at age ≤26, eligibility cannot be established. No Wikipedia biography.

name: Lea Verou
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Greek web-community company Fresset Ltd around 2007–2008 (registered 2008) at age ~21–22, building communities that later reached roughly 1% of Greece's population as registered users; by age 24 (2010) delivered a breakout first international conference talk at Front-Trends and by age 26 (2012) joined W3C as Developer Advocate / CSS Working Group invited expert.
early_history_summary: Born 13 June 1986 on Lesbos, Greece, to civil-engineer parents; only child who got a home PC in 1997 and taught herself programming via Multimedia Fusion then Visual Basic as a teen. After an unhappy start in electrical engineering in Thessaloniki, switched to CS at Athens University of Economics and Business while freelancing and building forums from 2005, then co-founded Fresset and became an internationally known CSS speaker.
primary_leverage_engine: Product/design taste and technical depth in CSS
family_context_summary: Grew up on Lesbos as an only child; parents were civil engineers and relatively well off (family bought an expensive PC in 1997). Mother died in 2013; Verou took her mother's surname officially.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were civil engineers, providing a technical household and resources for early computing tools, though not web-development domain expertise specifically.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early self-taught programming, Greek web communities, conference circuit, W3C, CSS depth
evidence_summary: Verou began serious computer making as a child and serious web freelancing by 19, co-founded a national-scale Greek web community company by 22, and broke into the international web-standards speaker circuit by 24. Family engineering background and ability to buy a mid-1990s PC supported early reps; online forums and blogs created distribution. Later W3C CSS Working Group invited expert role (from 2012), PrismJS, and the CSS Secrets book compounded that early stack.
starting_point: Born 1986 on Lesbos, Greece, to civil-engineer parents as an only child; relatively well-off household that provided a first personal computer in 1997.
current_position: HCI/usability researcher and consultant with a PhD from MIT; former W3C TAG member and CSS Working Group invited expert; Product Lead experience at Font Awesome; open to consulting (clients have included Google, Mozilla, Stripe).

trajectory.event: Began freelancing in web development and design while in university, after building and customizing online forums.
Co-founded Fresset Ltd around Greek web communities that later reached roughly 1% of Greece as registered users.
Delivered breakout first major international talk at Front-Trends and entered the global front-end conference circuit.
Joined W3C as Developer Advocate and became an invited expert on the CSS Working Group.
Published O'Reilly book CSS Secrets, later translated into multiple languages and widely cited as a top CSS title.
Completed multi-year W3C Technical Architecture Group service and continued MIT-linked research/consulting on creator tools and web usability.

name: John Boyer (software engineer)
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Born blind and later deafblind; graduated magna cum laude in math in 1961 at age 25, but first computer-programming course was 1964 (age 28) and defining open-source Braille tools (liblouis, BrailleBlaster) came decades later.
early_history_summary: Born in Wadena, Minnesota, fifth of twelve children of a farm-equipment business owner; born blind and lost hearing before age 10. Attended the New York Institute for the Blind, graduated high school as salutatorian (1956), then earned a BS in math magna cum laude from the College of St. Thomas (1961) with a note-taking translator.
family_context_summary: Fifth of twelve children; father owned a farm-equipment business in Wadena, Minnesota.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's farm-equipment business is not documented as conferring software or Braille-technology domain advantage.
evidence_summary: College graduation at 25 is academic success under extreme sensory constraints, but domain software contributions (liblouis commissioned 2002; BrailleBlaster 2010; White House Champion of Change 2012) occurred far after age 26.

name: Cal Henderson
milestone_by_age_26: As a core Ludicorp engineer and later chief software architect of Flickr, helped launch Flickr at O'Reilly ETech in 2004 (age 23) and scale it through Yahoo's 2005 acquisition (age 24); published O'Reilly's Building Scalable Web Sites in 2006 (age 25).
early_history_summary: Born Callum James Henderson-Begg on 17 January 1981 in the UK; attended Sharnbrook Upper School and graduated software engineering from Birmingham City University in 2002. Ran a Game Neverending fan site, broke into Ludicorp's internal mailing list, and was hired by Stewart Butterfield; co-created London web community B3ta and later cofounded Tiny Speck/Slack.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources beyond UK upbringing and schooling in Bedfordshire.
primary_early_advantage_tags: B3ta community, Ludicorp/Flickr, Butterfield partnership, Web 2.0 wave, early APIs
evidence_summary: Henderson combined early UK web-community work (B3ta, personal site since 2000) with a high-agency entry into Ludicorp via a fan site and mailing-list break-in that led to hiring. Partnership with Stewart Butterfield and complementary engineering peers produced Flickr's architecture and later Slack. Color blindness informed accessibility work; Web 2.0 photo-sharing and API waves provided structural leverage. Family financial/domain advantages are not documented.
starting_point: Born 1981 in the United Kingdom; educated at Sharnbrook Upper School and Birmingham City University; early involvement in London online communities.
current_position: Former co-founder and CTO of Slack (stepped down January 2024 after Salesforce acquisition); currently focused on advising and investing in software leaders; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.event: Graduated software engineering from Birmingham City University and soon joined Ludicorp after running a Game Neverending fan site.
Helped launch Flickr at O'Reilly ETech as a core engineer; service pioneered tagging, open APIs, and photo sharing at Web 2.0 scale.
Served as chief software architect as Flickr/Ludicorp was acquired by Yahoo.
Published O'Reilly book Building Scalable Web Sites based on Flickr engineering practice.
Co-founded Tiny Speck with Butterfield and others to build the game Glitch.
Internal Tiny Speck tooling pivoted into Slack, where he became co-founder and CTO.
Slack was acquired by Salesforce for about $27.7 billion.
Stepped down as Slack CTO; shifted focus to advising and investing.

name: Dale Heatherington
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Born 1948; co-founded Hayes Microcomputer Products and invented the PC modem / Hayes command set with Dennis Hayes in 1977 at age ~29. Age 26 was 1974, before the modem company.
early_history_summary: Studied electrical engineering at Southern Polytechnic State University; worked at Norman's Electronics and National Data Corporation, where he met Dennis Hayes. They pooled funds for an IMSAI 8080 and designed an early personal-computer modem, launching D.C. Hayes Associates / Hayes Microcomputer Products in 1977.
evidence_summary: Heatherington's defining achievement—co-founding Hayes and designing the Smartmodem lineage with the Hayes command set—is dated to 1977 when he was about 29. No material independently verified milestone by age 26 was found. Died in 2021.

name: Thomas Anantharaman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 verifiable. B.Tech from IIT (BHU) in 1982 (IIT-JEE rank ~#2 in 1977) and ChipTest/Deep Thought work at CMU began 1985, but public sources do not document a birth year, so age at those events cannot be confirmed as ≤26; computer-chess championship success is documented from 1987.
early_history_summary: Indian-born computer scientist, son of metallurgist T.R. Anantharaman; earned B.Tech in electronics (1982) from IIT BHU after a top IIT-JEE rank, then PhD at Carnegie Mellon (1990) working with Feng-hsiung Hsu on ChipTest and Deep Thought, foundations for IBM Deep Blue. Later moved into biostatistics and optical mapping at BioNano Genomics.
family_context_summary: Son of pre-eminent Indian metallurgist Tanjore Ramachandra Anantharaman (1927–2009); grew up in an academic scientific household. Exact birth year not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a leading materials scientist/metallurgist; strong scientific family culture but not computer-chess domain specifically.
evidence_summary: ChipTest/Deep Thought is a material scientific achievement, but without a documented birth year eligibility by age 26 cannot be established. Wikipedia marks year of birth as missing; conservative coding is ineligible.
